ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layer-Wise Gradient Cosine Between Text and Image Losses
PROPOSAL: Take a 1.5-billion-parameter autoregressive model trained under next-token prediction on interleaved text and VQ image tokens, and measure how its gradients disagree between modalities. On 2000 mixed batches, calculate the cosine between the gradient of the text-token loss and the gradient of the image-token loss for each transformer block, separately for attention and feed-forward weights. Report the mean and spread of the cosine against depth, and the fraction of batches with negative values.
CONTROLS: Cosine between two random halves of the text batch as a within-modality reference; cosine at a randomly initialised model; a repeat measurement after normalising each loss by its token count; and a second checkpoint to check stability.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: Cosines are lowest in the middle blocks and near zero or negative there, while same-modality references stay clearly positive. It could fail if the gap is mostly due to different loss magnitudes, which the normalised variant would show.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient Disagreement Tracked Through Training Checkpoints
PROPOSAL: Follow the gradients of a 1.5-billion-parameter autoregressive model trained on interleaved text and VQ image tokens at six saved checkpoints. At each one, draw 12000 mixed batches and obtain the cosine between text-loss and image-loss gradients per transformer block, for attention, feed-forward and normalisation weights, under three batch sizes. Report mean and spread of cosine by depth and the share of negative batches, split by attention, feed-forward and normalisation weights and by checkpoint.
CONTROLS: Same-modality cosine between halves of a text batch; a randomly initialised network; per-token normalisation of each loss; a second seed at each checkpoint, with confidence bands.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: Cosines are lowest in the middle blocks and near zero or negative there at all six checkpoints, while same-modality references stay clearly positive. It could fail if the three batch sizes give the same curves, so that extra settings add nothing.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Why Image Tokens and Text Tokens Conflict: Statistical Differences
PROPOSAL: Quantify how discretised image sequences differ from natural-language sequences and test whether these differences predict where gradients conflict. For a VQ tokenizer with a 16384-entry codebook, calculate per-position entropy, codebook usage skew, and the average mutual information between tokens at distances from one to sixty-four, on 200000 image sequences and 200000 text sequences of equal length. Relate each statistic to the layer-wise gradient cosine measured on the same data.
CONTROLS: A tokenizer trained with a smaller codebook; text shuffled at word level to remove order; image tokens shuffled in raster order; and rank correlation of each statistic with the cosine using permutation tests.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Image sequences show flatter codebook usage and longer-range dependence, and shuffling the order moves both statistics toward the text values. It could fail if the statistics are unrelated to the cosine profile, which would point to optimisation rather than data as the cause.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Statistics of Image Codes from Six Tokenizers and Their Link to Conflict
PROPOSAL: Characterise discretised image sequences against natural-language ones and ask whether the differences locate gradient conflict. Six VQ tokenizers with codebooks from 1024 to 65536 entries are examined for entropy by position, usage skew and mutual information at distances up to two hundred and fifty-six, over 2000000 image sequences and as many text sequences. Each statistic is then correlated with layer-wise gradient cosine obtained on matching data for every tokenizer, reporting the strongest predictor of the cosine profile in each depth band and the pooled ranking.
CONTROLS: Smaller-codebook retraining of one tokenizer; word-level text shuffling; raster-order image shuffling; permutation tests for the rank correlations, run separately per tokenizer.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Image sequences show flatter usage and longer-range dependence in all six tokenizers, and shuffling the order moves both statistics toward the text values. It could fail if statistics and cosine profile are unrelated, which would point to optimisation as the cause.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Modality-Specific Normalisation in a Fully Shared Autoregressive Transformer
PROPOSAL: Train a 1.5-billion-parameter autoregressive unified model from scratch on 300 billion tokens of text and VQ image data, where all attention and feed-forward weights are shared but each block owns separate normalisation scales and biases for text positions and image positions. Evaluate on four benchmarks, GenEval and DPG-Bench for generation, MMBench and POPE for understanding, and report layer-wise gradient cosine to show where conflict falls.
CONTROLS: A model with fully shared normalisation; a version with separate feed-forward experts in every block as a heavier alternative; a version with modality-specific scales just in the middle blocks; and equal-token training of all variants.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Separate normalisation raises the middle-block cosine and improves GenEval and MMBench relative to the shared model, while adding under one percent of parameters. It could fail if feed-forward experts recover far more, showing that normalisation alone cannot remove the conflict.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Placement of Modality-Specific Scales in a Seven-Billion-Parameter Unified Model
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a seven-billion-parameter autoregressive unified model on 1200 billion tokens of text and VQ image data with all main weights shared, giving separate normalisation scales to text and image positions in four alternative placements: first quarter, middle half, last quarter and all blocks. Score GenEval, DPG-Bench, MMBench, POPE and four reasoning sets, plus layer-wise gradient cosine, and report the gap to the shared model for each placement.
CONTROLS: A fully shared model; a model with separate feed-forward experts in all blocks; scales learned once for both modalities; the same token count for every variant.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Separate normalisation raises the middle-block cosine and improves GenEval and MMBench relative to the shared model, with the middle placement best. It could fail if the four placements land within noise of each other, so that placement is not worth tuning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does Modality-Aware Design Hold at Scale
PROPOSAL: Train two autoregressive unified models with a shared transformer at 1B, 3B and 7B parameters on 1 trillion tokens of text and VQ image data: a plain baseline, and its twin with modality-aware normalisation and loss weighting. Fit scaling curves of validation loss for text and for image tokens against training size and measure the gap between the two designs at each size. Evaluate GenEval, DPG-Bench and MMBench at the largest size.
CONTROLS: A baseline with tuned loss weights but no normalisation change; a baseline trained for equal wall-clock instead of equal tokens; two seeds at the smallest size to estimate run-to-run spread; and a second tokenizer at one size.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: The advantage of the modality-aware design in image-token loss persists or grows with size, with a smaller effect on text loss. It could fail if the gap closes at the largest size, which would show that the fix helps just small models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fitted Exponents of Plain and Modality-Aware Unified Models Over Six Sizes
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a plain and a modality-aware autoregressive unified model at six sizes between 0.5B and 7B parameters, each on 3 trillion tokens of mixed text and VQ image data, and fit power laws of text and image validation loss against training size. Compare exponents and offsets between the designs with bootstrap intervals over runs, then score GenEval, DPG-Bench and MMBench at the sizes nearest the ends and the middle of the range.
CONTROLS: Tuned loss weights without architecture change; equal wall-clock training instead of equal tokens; three seeds at each size under 3B for run-to-run spread; a different tokenizer at two sizes.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: Image-token loss advantage persists or grows with size, and fitted exponents differ between designs. It could fail if the six points lie on a single line within noise, so that exponent differences cannot be resolved.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient Surgery Versus Architectural Separation
PROPOSAL: Compare two ways of relieving modality conflict in a 1.5-billion-parameter autoregressive unified model: projecting conflicting gradients before each update, and giving the middle blocks separate normalisation for text and image positions. Train both from one initial checkpoint for 20 billion tokens, measure layer-wise gradient cosine, and evaluate GenEval and MMBench. Report training throughput per token, since gradient projection requires two backward passes.
CONTROLS: An unmodified model; loss-weight rebalancing alone; random gradient projection with matched probability, three draws; and the architectural variant with projection added on top to test whether the two effects combine.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The architectural variant matches or beats gradient projection on both benchmarks at higher throughput, and combining them adds little. It could fail if projection wins on image generation, which would indicate the conflict is partly an optimiser issue.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Four Conflict Remedies Under Three Learning Rates
PROPOSAL: Set four remedies against each other in a 1.5-billion-parameter autoregressive unified model: gradient projection, norm-based gradient rescaling, adaptive loss weighting, and separate middle-block normalisation for text and image positions. Starting from one shared checkpoint, train 80 billion tokens per remedy at each of three learning rates, then evaluate GenEval, DPG-Bench and MMBench, layer-wise gradient cosine and throughput.
CONTROLS: The unmodified model; static loss-weight rebalancing; random gradient projection at matched probability; the separate-normalisation variant combined with projection, at each learning rate.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Separate normalisation matches or beats projection on all benchmarks at higher throughput, and combining them adds little. It could fail if the ranking of remedies flips with the learning rate, which would make single-setting comparisons unreliable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Where in Depth Should Modalities Be Separated
PROPOSAL: Locate the depth range where modality separation pays off. In a 1.5-billion-parameter autoregressive unified model with 24 blocks, give text positions and image positions separate low-rank adapters in one contiguous window of 6 blocks, and slide the window across the stack in steps of 6. Train each variant for 30 billion tokens, and compare GenEval, MMBench and layer-wise gradient cosine against the window position.
CONTROLS: A fully shared model; adapters in all blocks at equal total rank; one adapter set applied to both modalities in the best window; and three windows chosen at random at matched size.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Windows in the middle of the stack give the largest gains, while first and last windows give almost none. It could fail if adapters in all blocks beat every window, showing that conflict is spread across depth.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Window Position and Width for Modality Adapters in a Deeper Stack
PROPOSAL: Map where modality separation pays off in a 3-billion-parameter autoregressive unified model with 36 blocks. Text positions and image positions receive separate low-rank adapters inside a contiguous window whose width runs from 2 to 12 blocks and whose start moves in steps of 2. Train each variant on 60 billion tokens; GenEval, DPG-Bench, MMBench and layer-wise gradient cosine are plotted against position and width.
CONTROLS: A fully shared model; adapters in all blocks at equal total rank; a single adapter set serving both modalities in the best window; three randomly drawn windows of matched size.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Windows in the middle of the stack give the largest gains, first and last windows almost none, and widths beyond six add little. It could fail if adapters in all blocks beat the best window, showing that conflict is spread across depth.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Representation Similarity Between Modalities at Each Depth
PROPOSAL: Check whether text and image positions of an autoregressive unified model trained under next-token loss are represented in compatible ways at each depth. Feed 5000 caption-image pairs, extract internal activations at every block for text positions and image positions, and calculate linear centred kernel alignment between the two sets, and the accuracy of a linear probe trained on text states and tested on image states for object category. Plot both against depth.
CONTROLS: A shuffled-pairing control that matches captions to wrong images; a randomly initialised model; probes trained and tested within one modality as a ceiling; and a second checkpoint from a different seed.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Alignment and cross-modal probe accuracy peak in the middle blocks and drop near the output, matching the depth where gradient conflict is strongest. It could fail if alignment is flat in depth, so representation similarity does not explain the conflict.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Alignment of Text and Image Activations in Four Training Snapshots
PROPOSAL: Ask whether text and image positions of unified autoregressive models share a compatible code, using four training snapshots. Pass 20000 caption-image pairs through each, read out activations from all blocks, and obtain linear and RBF kernel alignment between the modalities, along with cross-modal linear probes for object category, colour and count. Everything is plotted against depth, with the peak location and its width reported for each snapshot and probe target.
CONTROLS: Captions matched to wrong images; a randomly initialised model; same-modality probes as ceiling; three seeds per snapshot.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Alignment and cross-modal accuracy peak in the middle blocks and fall near the output at all four snapshots, matching the depth of strongest gradient conflict. It could fail if the two kernels and three probe targets disagree on where the peak lies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training Efficiency of a Modality-Aware Unified Model
PROPOSAL: Test whether respecting modality differences speeds up training. Train a 3-billion-parameter autoregressive unified model, in plain and modality-aware forms, on 500 billion tokens, and log the number of training tokens needed to reach fixed validation losses for text and image tokens and fixed GenEval scores. Report the speed-up factor at each target and the total effort of reaching the plain model's final quality.
CONTROLS: A plain model trained with a longer warm-up; a plain model with tuned peak learning rate; the modality-aware model without its loss weighting; and the plain model with three seeds to measure spread of the token counts.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: The modality-aware model reaches each target with fewer tokens, with a speed-up of a clear factor that grows with the target quality. It could fail if tuning the plain model's learning rate closes most of the gap.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Token-Efficiency Race Under Four Data Mixtures
PROPOSAL: Ask whether respecting modality differences reaches a given quality sooner. Train a 7-billion-parameter autoregressive unified model in plain and modality-aware forms on 1500 billion tokens under four text-to-image mixture ratios, noting the tokens consumed before text loss, image loss, GenEval and MMBench cross fixed targets. State the speed-up at each target and the training needed to match the plain model's final quality, with a separate table for each mixture ratio and a pooled summary.
CONTROLS: Longer warm-up for the plain model; tuned peak learning rate for the plain model; the modality-aware model without loss weighting; three seeds of the plain model under each mixture.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: The modality-aware model crosses each target with fewer tokens in all four mixtures, with a speed-up that grows with target quality. It could fail if the mixtures with more image data show no speed-up.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer of the Modality-Aware Design to Image Editing
PROPOSAL: Test whether a modality-aware autoregressive unified model keeps its advantage when fine-tuned for instruction-based image editing. Starting from plain and modality-aware 1.5-billion-parameter checkpoints, fine-tune on 150000 editing triples of source image, instruction and target image, then evaluate on GEdit-Bench and ImgEdit, and report source-consistency measured by a perceptual distance on unedited regions.
CONTROLS: Fine-tuning the plain checkpoint with matched learning rate; fine-tuning with the source image tokens masked from the loss; a diffusion-based editor as an external reference; and human preference by three raters on 300 edits.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: The modality-aware checkpoint scores higher on both editing benchmarks and preserves unedited regions better. It could fail if editing quality is limited by the tokenizer's reconstruction error, so the architectural difference vanishes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Editing and Question Answering After Mixed Fine-Tuning of Both Designs
PROPOSAL: Ask whether the modality-aware advantage survives fine-tuning that mixes editing and question answering. Starting from plain and modality-aware 3-billion-parameter checkpoints, fine-tune on 600000 editing triples together with 400000 question items, evaluate on GEdit-Bench, ImgEdit, MMBench and POPE, and report source-consistency by a perceptual distance on unedited regions.
CONTROLS: Matched learning rate for the plain checkpoint; masking source image tokens from the loss; a diffusion editor as external reference; human preference on 1200 edits, scored by three raters in random order.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: The modality-aware checkpoint scores higher on both editing benchmarks and preserves unedited regions better, with a smaller gain on question answering. It could fail if question data dominate the mixed fine-tune and erase the editing difference.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Validating the Conflict Metric on a Toy Two-Task Transformer
PROPOSAL: Before applying the layer-wise gradient measure to a unified model, validate it on a transformer with four blocks trained on two synthetic sequence tasks whose degree of overlap is controlled by the fraction of shared vocabulary. At 11 overlap levels, calculate the per-block gradient cosine between the two task losses and check that it increases monotonically with overlap. Report rank correlation and the block where the metric is most sensitive.
CONTROLS: Two copies of one task, for which cosine must be near one; two tasks with disjoint vocabularies and unrelated labels, for which it must be near zero; and a version with noisy gradients from a tiny batch size.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: The cosine rises with overlap in every block, near one for identical tasks and near zero for disjoint ones. It could fail if small batches make the estimate too noisy to rank blocks, so the metric needs larger batches.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Metric Validation on Toy Transformers with Four, Eight and Sixteen Blocks
PROPOSAL: Validate the layer-wise gradient measure on toy transformers of four, eight and sixteen blocks, each trained on two synthetic sequence tasks whose overlap is set by the share of common vocabulary. For 21 overlap levels and five seeds, obtain the per-block cosine between the two task losses and test that it grows monotonically with overlap. Report rank correlation and the most sensitive block for each depth, together with the spread across seeds and the overlap level at which the cosine first exceeds one half.
CONTROLS: Identical tasks, where cosine must be near one; tasks with disjoint vocabularies and unrelated labels, where it must be near zero; noisy gradients from three tiny batch sizes.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: The cosine rises with overlap in every block at all three depths, near one for identical tasks and near zero for disjoint ones. It could fail if the most sensitive block moves with depth, in which case the metric needs a depth-aware reading.
